NaAudio__Space__Meta.Name: First Space
NaAudio__Space__Meta.Description: The demonstration arrangement AudioSPACE opens with. A circular sequencer on a CR-78 kit, a CubeMod playing a pentatonic figure through its own synth voice, and a DelayCloud processing both. Authored as data rather than as a bootstrap function, so a new arrangement is a JSON edit.
NaAudio__Space__Meta.Author: Adam Noble - Noble Architecture
NaAudio__Space__Meta.LayoutNote: Positions are in metres on the ground plane, with the listener at the origin. The three instruments sit on a ring facing the centre, roughly 4.5 metres out - close enough to read a step from the middle of the space, far enough apart that no two cages overlap. The output post stands at the origin, so every lead runs inward and the middle of the space is where the signal collects.
NaAudio__Space__Meta.RoutingNote: A module bus reaches the speakers ONLY through a cable into an OutputPost. Nothing connects itself to the master any more, so a space file with no path to a post loads correctly and is completely silent. This arrangement is deliberately the same signal flow the first build had by default: the sequencer and the cube are heard dry AND through the cloud, which is why each of them has two leads.

Settings.PostNote: The way out of the space. Its audio input is the master bus itself, so a lead into this post is the difference between a module being audible and being silent. Standing it at the origin puts it on the listener datum, which is the one place in the space that already meant 'where the sound arrives'.

Settings.PatternNote: One character per division, read left to right from twelve o'clock clockwise. 'x' is a hit and '.' is a rest. Written this way so the pattern is legible at a glance in an editor - an array of sixteen booleans is not.

Settings.SelfPlayNote: A CubeMod is a controller, so on its own it is silent and impossible to evaluate. Set false to stop it playing its own walking figure and drive it from a sequencer instead.

Settings.SeedNote: Seeds the sphere start positions and velocities, so this space reopens looking as it was left rather than rescattered.

NaAudio__Space__Cables.Note: The sequencer's drums into the enclosure, so resizing the box audibly changes the space the kit sits in.
Two sources into one effect, which is what the design manifest asks the routing to support.
The dry drums. Unplug this and the kit is only heard through the cloud, which is the quickest demonstration in the space of what the post actually decides.

The wet return. Everything that goes into the enclosure leaves the space through here, so this is the one lead that must never be pulled by accident - which is exactly why unplugging needs wiring mode.
